title: Kernel ABI flapping and opcache inventory
body:
Summary:

This is a working log for an odd latency regression we've been seeing in the field on mixed-length workloads. Symptoms: intermittent 2–6x single-request tail latency spikes on models using FlashAttention fused ops, concentrated on hosts with AggressiveOpCache enabled. The pattern looks like 'kernel ABI flapping' — repeated small failures/path changes inside the fused-op loader that cause a fallback to paged or plain kernels, then a fast re-load of the optimized kernel, producing jitter.

Goals for this doc:
- Capture repro cases and microbench commands.
- List observations from traces and perf counters.
- Inventory opcache entries and ABI mismatch candidates.
- Quick mitigations and next experiments.

High-level hypothesis (working):
- The runtime's opcache stores compiled kernels keyed by an ABI fingerprint that includes device compute capability, model configuration flags, and a kernel-recipe version.
- Under load and with varying sequence lengths, memory pressure + ephemeral worker restarts cause opcache entries to be invalidated or evicted. When the loader tries to validate a candidate, small ABI-compatibility checks fail (mismatched launch bounds or register usage flagged by driver), causing a fallback to a slower kernel. Immediately afterward, a hot path triggers a recompile/selection of the fused kernel which briefly restores fast performance. This flapping shows as latency oscillation.

Repro steps (microbench):
1) Baseline environment:
   - Node: g5.2xlarge equivalent, CUDA 12.1, driver 540.xx, cuBLAS 13.1, torch-cu121 from wheel.
   - Build: serving-runtime@main (commit sha: e5b7c3f) with AggressiveOpCache=true, OpCacheSize=256MB.

2) Repro script (local):
   - run: python tests/bench/mixed_seq_burst.py --model llama-small --batch-dist "[8x32,50x8,2x256]" --qps 120 --duration 10m --heat 20s
   - enable tracing: /opt/runtime/bin/tracectl --nsys --out=trace-mixedseq

3) Expected outcome:
   - 95th/99th latency spikes every 30–60s correlated with kernel log lines in runtime.log: "opcache: validate failed (ABI mismatch) for key=..." then fallback lines, then later "opcache: compiled candidate ok".

Observed traces and counters:
- NSYS traces show repeated kernel launch attempts for fused_attention.forward (same symbol name) with varying grid sizes. Pattern: small launch returns illegal memory access code (cudaErrorIllegalAddress) quickly, then fallback to paged_attention that runs for the bulk of the step.
- /proc/driver/nvlink or nvidia-smi did not show GPU resets; errors originate at kernel validation stage in our runtime (the runtime queries PTX attributes and compares with expected resource limits).
- Perf counters (from nvprof/metrics): IPC dips during fallback windows; SM occupancy is lower on fallback kernels but memory throughput higher (due to paging).
- Sampling logs from the fused-op build: objdump inspection shows two candidate kernels with different PTX compute_ capability annotations (sm_86 vs sm_80) — mismatch arises when host toolchain injects a conservative code path for sm_80 but runtime expects sm_86.

Quick inventory (opcache):
- opcache listing command added: /opt/runtime/bin/opcachectl list --verbose
- Example output lines we see repeatedly: 
   key: fused_attn_v2#recipe-17#sm_86#flags=QK_INT8,launch=compact
   key: fused_attn_v2#recipe-17#sm_80#flags=QK_INT8,launch=compact
   validate: recipe-17 -> rejected: "registers=90 expected<=64"

This shows that multiple ABI variants exist in cache for the same logical kernel. Our validation currently compares a small set of attributes; a corner-case mismatch on register usage leads to rejection.

Root-cause candidates (ranked):
1) Toolchain nondeterminism: our JIT path uses nvcc/rocm frontend flags that can produce slightly different register allocation across invocations on the same machine when CPU load and memory layout changes.
2) ABI fingerprint too strict/too loose: we either reject safe variants (causing fallback even though kernels would run) or accept incompatible variants that then fault. Current fingerprint doesn't include "max_registers" leading to mismatches.
3) Eviction policy thrash: small OpCacheSize + ephemeral allocations cause eviction and immediate recompilation under load, producing temporary states where kernel metadata races with actual binary blob presence.
4) Mixed runtime flags: an A/B rollout of a fused-op recipe (recipe-17 vs recipe-18) across workers leading to cross-host key collisions when moving worker tasks.

Short-term mitigation options (to test):
- Turn off AggressiveOpCache on a limited canary pool (INF-2124). Preliminary internal rollouts reduced 99th latency but raised token-cost by ~4% because more recompiles happened off-path.
- Make validation more conservative: if metadata mismatch is only in register usage (<= 16 reg diff), try a dry-run launch with small workload to confirm instead of immediate reject. Implement as runtime flag: OpCacheRelaxedValidation=true.
- Increase OpCacheSize for hosts showing heavy flapping and observe eviction rate.
- Pin fused-op recipe per worker (no cross-recipe acceptance) as temporary stopgap.

Longer experiments to run:
- Reproduce with deterministic toolchain: build fused kernels inside a container with isolated CPU affinity and memory layout to confirm nondeterminism hypothesis. Use perf record to see if JIT passes differ.
- Add a "soft-validate" mode where the runtime tries to run the candidate on a tiny synthetic batch (seq len 8, batch 1) and only if it passes, mark valid. This trades a tiny extra latency on first use for correctness.
- Add stronger cache keys: include register pressure, shared-memory usage, and PTX version string. Also add a checksum of the binary blob.
- Stress test eviction policy: synthetic workload that cycles hot-key sets to observe evict/compile churn.

Data collected so far (summary numbers):
- Canary with AggressiveOpCache=true (baseline): 99p_latency=180ms, spikes to 900ms intermittently. Evictions/min=12
- Canary with AggressiveOpCache=false: 99p_latency=115ms, fewer spikes, evictions/min=2, but average compile CPU usage +18%.
- Experiment with OpCacheSize=1GB on same node: spikes cut in half, evictions/min=3.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Aisha: add opcache list and dump to startup logs for next week (INF-2124).
- Marco: prototype OpCacheRelaxedValidation and a dry-run-launch path (PR draft on github link above). Target: perf impact <0.5% on cold path.
- Priya: run deterministic build container and produce two independent compiler outputs for comparison.
- SRE: allocate 4 nodes with OpCacheSize increased to 1GB for one hour test.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do some hosts never show flapping? Are driver microversions subtly different? Need a binary-level diff of nvidia driver strings across fleet.
- Is there a race between opcache metadata update and file sync when using network-backed cache (NFS)? We saw correlated anomalies on nodes running NFS-mounted /var/cache.
- Does quantization flag combination (int8 vs int4) increase register pressure leading to spurious reject?

Notes / context / references:
- Related Linear ticket: INF-2124 (kernel ABI flapping investigation)
- Early thread: slack #eng-serving-runtime (thread id: D12J4F7)
- Previous work on opcache eviction heuristics: doc located at /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/opcache-eviction-playbook.json (see linked artifacts)

Appendix: useful commands and quick parsers
- opcache list: /opt/runtime/bin/opcachectl list --json > /tmp/opcache.json
- quick grep of runtime logs for flapping: 
  grep -E "opcache: (validate failed|compiled candidate|evicted)" /var/log/serving-runtime/runtime.log | tail -n 200
- trace to find the moment of fallback: open trace-mixedseq.nsys in Nsight Systems and filter on fused_attention.forward symbol.

Draft notes end — please add reproducer traces or observations below as comments.
